name: Sable & Fork Food Service Uniform Set
description:
Sable & Fork is the dominant supplier of food service uniforms across GLMZ's restaurant and catering industry, covering everything from Tier 2 canteens to Tier 4 corporate dining facilities. The standard set includes a double-breasted chef's coat, work trousers, and an apron, all constructed from a heat-resistant synthetic-cotton blend rated to sustained exposure at 280°C without degradation. The coat is white with black piping at the collar and cuff — a deliberate neutral that allows restaurants to add their own branding through embroidery or heat-transfer patches. The apron is a heavier canvas weave with a grease-resistant coating that repels most organic and synthetic cooking oils; it can be wiped clean during a shift and machine-washed at the end. The trouser design includes wide-leg construction to avoid heat trapping near open flame or induction surfaces.

Sable & Fork's geneware accommodation is notably thorough for food service wear, driven by the reality that kitchen workforces in M88 are highly diverse. The coat includes a rear yoke panel that opens for tail clearance, the collar sits low enough to avoid friction with common neck augments, and the hat options include a structured toque with horn-clearance inserts as well as a close-fit net cap designed for fur-bearing head configurations — both rated as equivalent hygienic coverage under GLMZ's food safety code. The uniform set is priced at the lower end of Sable & Fork's range; higher-tier establishments typically order the structured Maison line, but the standard set is what keeps M88's food industry running.
cultural_context: The Sable & Fork white-and-black is the invisible uniform of M88 — worn by the people who feed the city, rarely seen by the people being fed. In Tier 1 and 2 communities, the uniform is associated with one of the few stable employment sectors available, and the condition of someone's Sable & Fork set is often a quiet indicator of how long they've held the job: new and stiff, or soft and stained with the specific colors of a particular kitchen.
story_hooks: A kitchen worker at a Tier 4 corporate dining facility discovers their apron's grease-resistant coating is also filtering trace compounds from the food being prepared — someone is adding something to the menu that isn't on the ingredient list.

A Sable & Fork distribution center is found to be shipping uniform sets with embedded RFID tags that aren't in the product spec — someone is using the uniforms to track food service workers across the city.
A chef's coat recovered from a crime scene carries embroidery from a restaurant that was destroyed in a fire three years ago — but the coat's fabric shows no age consistent with that timeline.

physical_description.visual_profile: A crisp, utilitarian ensemble designed for high-heat kitchen environments. The silhouette is clean and functional — the double-breasted chef's coat creates a structured, authoritative front, while the wide-leg trousers provide a deliberate loose fit that reads as both practical and subtly professional. The overall impression is of competent uniformity: deliberately neutral, meant to fade into the background of a working kitchen.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and spacious throughout. The coat is cut for layering and movement; sleeves are rolled-ready with reinforced cuffs. Trousers are wide-leg with a high waist, designed to sit clear of heat sources and allow unrestricted motion. The apron hangs straight from the shoulders without cinching the torso.
physical_description.primary_material: Heat-resistant synthetic-cotton blend (rated 280°C continuous exposure). Apron is a heavier grease-resistant canvas weave with hydrophobic coating.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly stiff when new with a subtle textile sheen from the synthetic fibers. Canvas apron has a visible weave texture and matte finish. Both materials develop soft patina with repeated washing and kitchen exposure.
physical_description.color_scheme: Stark white as primary, with black piping along the collar and cuffs. Apron is natural canvas with darker staining patterns (oil, char, food residue) that develop over time. No decorative pattern — branding space left intentionally blank for restaurant customization via embroidery or heat-transfer.
physical_description.closures: Double-breasted button front on the coat (traditional white buttons, often replaced after heavy use). Apron fastens with neck loop and waist ties in black cotton twill. Trousers feature a standard fly with button closure.
distinctive_features: Rear yoke panel with opening for tail clearance — geneware accommodation
Low-sitting collar designed to avoid friction with neck augmentation hardware
Reinforced cuffs rated for repeated hot-water washing
Grease-resistant canvas apron with deep front pocket for tools and towels
Wide-leg trouser cut to prevent heat trapping near open flame or induction surfaces
Toque and close-fit net cap options included — both with augmentation-specific sizing
Blank front chest area reserved for restaurant branding patches
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional. This is the standard-issue uniform, accessible to entry-level kitchen staff and mid-career food service workers. Higher tiers wear the Sable & Fork Maison line with additional tailoring and premium materials.
physical_description.cultural_context: This uniform signals stable, blue-collar employment in GLMZ's essential food service sector. Worn by the invisible workers who feed the metropolitan zone — rare sight to Tier 1 residents, but ubiquitous in working-class neighborhoods. The condition of the set (crisp and new vs. soft and stained) is a quiet autobiography of employment tenure and kitchen assignment.
physical_description.condition_typical: Varies dramatically by wearer. New uniforms arrive pristine and stiff. After weeks of service, the white dulls slightly, black piping softens, and the apron develops organic staining patterns — char marks, oil shadows, coffee rings — that are nearly impossible to completely remove. Long-term wearers' uniforms become soft, slightly faded, with visible rewashing wear at collar and cuffs. Most Sable & Fork sets are replaced annually, though kitchen veterans often request their old sets be retired rather than reassigned.

image_prompt: Fashion photography of a Sable & Fork food service uniform set displayed on a dark mannequin or worn by a cyberpunk-styled figure with subtle augmentations visible at neck and hands. The double-breasted white chef's coat is crisp with black piping at collar and cuffs; wide-leg work trousers hang clean and functional; a grease-resistant canvas apron drapes from the shoulders. Moody industrial kitchen lighting casts sharp shadows across the white fabric, emphasizing texture and practical design. Background is a blurred GLMZ urban kitchen or service corridor — stainless steel, warm overhead lights, wet concrete. The uniform reads as both anonymous and essential, clean but clearly designed for work. Slight visible wear or aging preferred to show authenticity.
